Bees are primarily known for producing honey, beeswax, propolis, royal jelly, and pollen. Honey serves as their food source and is harvested by humans for its sweet flavor and preservative qualities. Beeswax is used by bees to construct honeycomb structures for storing honey and raising brood, and it is also widely used in candles, cosmetics, and polishes. Propolis is a resinous mixture collected from tree buds and used by bees to seal gaps in the hive and protect against pathogens. Royal jelly is a secretion fed to queen bees and larvae, while pollen is collected as a protein source.
